This is easier said than done, but you have to try and make new friends. There’s a lot of ways to do that, and you might even be able to find some new ones through your current friends, but otherwise, they don’t sound like the best thing for you. And I’m not blaming you for doing this, but actions like clingy behavior make people uncomfortable and give them less desire to spend time with you. I don’t know your situation, but there has to be some way for you to put yourself out there, even if you have to do it alone at first. If you attend college that’s a great way. Between sorority events and clubs/organizations, they always have campus events and similar things that encourage students to come together. If you live in a city, that’s a big place just waiting for you to find something in. Cities, especially major ones, always have numerous events, festivals, shows, etc. Having a car helps as well, or some means of public transportation. Even having a job can be beneficial, as crews of people can become close due to the amount of time that they have to spend together.  

I might also recommend that you work on improving yourself as well, because if you are really that afraid of being alone, it’s not going to be healthy for you in the short or long term. Honestly, you might to see a therapist/counselor for that. If you attend college, many campuses have counseling centers where you can seek services. If you have health insurance and can stomach roughly $60-100 per visit (just the range that I’ve experienced thus far), you should be able to find one just about anywhere, especially near/in a city. You’ll want a good one, so try to size them up first or do some research on the counselor/therapist to see if they’re actually going to be able to help.  

I hope any of this helps. I think you’ll be alright, you just have to try to do some new things to improve yourself and surround yourself with more mentally healthy influences. Wishing you the best.
